_confirmation: agent-confirmed, not human-reviewed (owner delegated confirmation on 2026-10-15; to be reviewed once at the next milestone)
_buckets: Decisions: required (must appear), excluded (FAIL if present), unlisted (everything else: reported + reviewed on dev, never auto-failed). Risks/reuse: allowed = relevant and acceptable; anything else is unlisted/review.
_precedence: excluded_subjects are checked first and win over allowed_subjects (globs use fnmatch: '*' crosses '/').
_excluded_provenance: excluded_subjects were drafted AFTER the author had seen output of the earlier rule-based (pre-LLM, commit a7fccfa) planner, which listed bus-factor risks about unrelated werkzeug datastructures files and unrelated libraries for these requests. They are therefore informed by that output and are used on DEV cases only. Held-out cases have no excluded_subjects; their unlisted risks and reuse are reported as counts only.
_scope: DEV cases only. Held-out scoring is separate and counts-only.

cases.request: Change markupsafe escape() so it also escapes backtick characters
cases.unlisted_note: ADR-101 moved from 'allowed' to unlisted (review). Consistent rule: ADR-101 applies when the request changes the VERSION of a Pallets package (as in the held-out Jinja upgrade case); a behaviour change inside markupsafe only reaches that rule when it is released and consumers bump it, which the request does not ask for.

allowed_subjects.why: Procedure for shipping a markupsafe change

excluded_subjects.why: Header/ETag/Accept structures do not call escape() (appeared as bus-factor noise in the old plan); wins over the broad werkzeug consumer glob

HTTP client: no escaping involved
HTTP transport: no escaping involved
Signing library: no escaping involved
